recipes.name: Seven Layer Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 large head iceberg lettuce - rinsed, dried, and chopped
1 (10 ounce) package frozen green peas, thawed

steps.text: Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels; crumble and set aside.
To make the salad: Place chopped lettuce in a large glass dish or bowl; top with a layer of red onion, peas, shredded cheese, cauliflower, and bacon.
To make the dressing: Whisk mayonnaise, Parmesan cheese, and sugar together in a bowl until smooth.
Drizzle dressing over salad and refrigerate until chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Seven Layer Salad
raw_recipe.description: Make this 7-layer salad in a large glass bowl so dinner guests can see all the pretty layers and delicious ingredients. Everybody loves this salad!

video.description: Try this staple recipe of the seventies that combines so many delicious flavors and textures together in one dish. In this video, Nicole makes vintage seven layer salad. Each layer contains a different ingredient, starting with chopped iceberg lettuce. After adding the lettuce, go layer by layer adding chopped red onion, green peas, grated sharp cheddar cheese, chopped cauliflower, dressing, and chopped bacon. This vintage seven layer salad is a perfect side dish for any potluck, barbecue, or family gathering.
video.name: How to Make Vintage Seven Layer Salad

review.reviewBody: This is an awesome recipe. Comments were made about the dressing being to thick. My aunt gave me this same recipe but the dressing uses 1 cup mayo and 1 cup sour cream and of course the parmesan cheese and sugar. It makes a creamy dressing and is easier to spread and is soooo good. My family just loves it.

I was looking for new ways to get veggies into my husband. He likes a lot of raw, but not cooked vegetables. I made this recipe yesterday and my husband & I loved it! Changes I would make next time: *use 1 C mayo & 1 C sourcream instead of 1 1/4 C mayo
*add 3 chopped, boiled eggs *add a tablespoon of white vinegar to mayo & sourcream mixture *as a finishing touch, add extra crumbled bacon and shredded (not grated) parmesean cheese & 1/2 C of toasted, chopped pecans. Changes I made yesterday: *I used 1/2 of a large, sweet onion instead of a red onion (it was too strong) *I used shredded Parmesean cheese to the mayo

This is an excellent recipe. Because the dressing is rather thick when first prepared, it should read "spread" the dressing instead of "drizzle" it over the salad. It thins after sitting and then being tossed with the vegetable mixture. This salad can be prepared and refrigerated 8-12 hours before serving. I substituted Swiss cheese instead of Cheddar, and added 3 chopped hard boiled eggs and 1 cup of chopped celery. I love recipes that can be made-up ahead of time!
I made this for a party recently and it was a big hit. The only change I would make is to layer the dressing in the salad instead of just adding it to the top.

My sister in law always made layered salad, but I was never impressed. The glob of mayo on top turned me off & it always felt like it needed mixed up to avoid a bite of one ingredient. Then my friend came over for a cook out & I watched her mix up a salad, lettuce, mozzerella cheese, eggs bacon, peas & optional onions. She then tossed it all with the mayo/sugar dressing. OMG it was amazing. I started making it this way & my inlaws & parents declared it their favorite salad & request at all get togethers. Just throwing this out as an alternative to a great salad. BTW mayo goes on right before serving & make sure lettuce is dry to avoid being runny. I rinse lettuce the day before & dry in fridge with paper towels.

I love the simple but delicious dressing. I make mine in a 9x13 glass cake pan. It's easier to serve and get all the layers. How I layer is with these ingredients. Lettuce, red onion, fresh broccoli, 3 hard boiled eggs, then the mayo mixture. Then I top that with the cheddar cheese and the bacon on top.

I used another reviewer's suggestion of thinning the dressing. I mixed 2/3 cup of Greek plain yogurt with 2/3 cup of mayo, 1 tb. of white sugar and 1/3 cup of parmesan cheese. It came out so tasty I started eating a few spoonfuls before adding to the salad! I spooned out the dressing in the center of the salad and barely had to spread it to the sides. I then refrigerated and let the dressing slowly percolate through the top layers. This is the second time I made this and definitely plan on a third.

Excellent recipe. The dressing is forgiving, so you can use more or less of any ingredients -- I didn't have Parmesan on hand, so I added a bit of garlic powder and salt instead. I recommend using a wide, flat dish, such as a casserole dish, so that it's easier to scoop and serve. (It does look "prettier" in a trifle dish, but it makes it far more difficult to scoop out and get all of the ingredients onto your plate.)
I highly recommend layering it in the following order, especially if you're making this recipe more than a few hours in advance: 
Lettuce (I used Romaine),
Peas,
Cauliflower,
Onion (I omitted this),
Dressing,
Cheddar Cheese,
Tomato,
Bacon. 
Layering in this order ensures the bacon stays dry and crispy on top, the salad sticks together better when you're scooping it, and the dressing settles in closer to the veggies--where you need it! :-)

I've made a version of this salad for 50 years. Mine has no cauliflower and no parmesan cheese in the mayo. In fact, in these parts we just sprinkle sugar over the mayo layer. Chill for a few hours or overnight. I like to stir it together when I serve it so dressing and ingredients are dispersed throughout. I use sweet onions (such as Vidalia) instead of red. Some people put a layer of chopped hard boiled eggs in as well.

Amazing the raves I get with this one. I think it's the parmesan in the dressing that makes it stand out from other recipes like this. The only change I made was that I wanted boiled eggs in my salad, but didn't want to take any of the other ingredients out. So it's an 8-layer salad!

I have a BnB in Italy, and I make this for our weekly Pizza Nigh,t and it is always a hit. I do make a few tweaks by doubling the dressing recipe and adding a few tablespoons of cider vinegar for a little acid. I put a layer of dressing in the middle as well as on top. I also add layers of cooked beets, crumbled blue cheese, and hard-boiled eggs. Everyone asks for the recipe!

This is very difficult to serve in such a high sided bowl. Much better to put in rectangular dish like you would use for lasagna. Just do thinner layers . It's much wasier to serve with large spoon and not have to dig down in a high sided bowl
I made sure to make enough dressing to slather some on each layer before i put the next layer on. Then added additional parm on to and also cut tomato wedges on top of bacon. Yum
I can eat this every day

I love the recipe as is but many of my family can't do onions well so I half or quarter the onion depending on where I'm taking it. I think next time I will use a couple green onions on top instead of red as a layer.

The dressing is too sweet and the addition of parmesan doesn't help. I used lettuce, then shredded carrots, sliced cucumbers, then frozen peas, then a can of corn, then a can of shoestring pickled beets, topped with dressing, garnished with sprinkles of shredded cheese and a few sliced black olives.
Great for a crowd!
Yummy
Turned out beautiful. Great flavors. Love the simple dressing.
I like it and I try it out
